If the party shall inform immediately after, then (as intended compliance) it informs immediately after.
Non-parties have no right under Dutch Civil Code section 6:253 to enforce or benefit from the Agreement.
constraints.reasoning: Explicitly stated exclusion of third-party rights.

constraints.translation: The Agreement may be executed in counterpart.
If it is executed in counterpart, then it may be executed in counterpart.
constraints.reasoning: If something occurs, then it is (at least) possible/permitted; logical strengthening.

constraints.translation: A facsimile or pdf signature shall be deemed an original.
If it shall be deemed an original, then (as intended effect) it is deemed an original.
Notices may be served by delivery, prepaid first-class post, or fax.
If a notice is served via those methods, then it falls within the 'may be served' permission.
constraints.reasoning: Occurrence implies the method is among permitted/possible service methods described.

constraints.translation: A notice is effective only when actually received.
constraints.reasoning: "Shall be effective only when" is mandatory and exclusive.

constraints.translation: If effectiveness is required only upon actual receipt, then (as intended rule) notice effectiveness depends on actual receipt.
constraints.reasoning: Normative-to-descriptive inference about the effectiveness condition.

constraints.translation: If a notice is effective only when actually received, then it is not effective when not actually received.
constraints.reasoning: Direct logical exclusion from the phrase 'effective only when actually received'.

constraints.translation: Any communication under/in connection with the Agreement shall be in writing.
If communications shall be in writing, then (as intended compliance) communications are in writing.
Unless otherwise stated, communications may be by e-mail or letter.
If communications are made by e-mail or letter, then they are within the permitted methods.
constraints.reasoning: Occurrence implies the method is among those permitted/possible methods described.

constraints.translation: If communications may be by e-mail or letter, then communications are to be in writing (email/letter are written forms).
constraints.reasoning: Common-sense semantic relation: emails and letters are written communications; text presents them in the context of the writing requirement.

constraints.translation: The Agreement shall be governed by the laws of The Netherlands.
If it shall be governed by Dutch law, then (as intended legal effect) it is governed by Dutch law.
If governed by Dutch law, then it is not governed by English law or New York law.
constraints.reasoning: Mutual exclusivity: a contract's governing law is typically a single choice among legal systems.

constraints.translation: The competent court in The Hague shall have exclusive jurisdiction.
constraints.reasoning: "Shall have exclusive jurisdiction" is mandatory and exclusive.

constraints.translation: If The Hague court shall have exclusive jurisdiction, then (as intended effect) it has exclusive jurisdiction.
If exclusive jurisdiction is in The Hague, then exclusive jurisdiction is not in Amsterdam, London, or New York.
constraints.evidence: Jurisdiction clause (exclusive jurisdiction in The Hague)
constraints.reasoning: Mutual exclusivity of 'exclusive jurisdiction' across distinct forums.

constraints.translation: Disclosures falling under the permissions in Clauses 4 or 7 are not unauthorized disclosures.
constraints.evidence: Clause 2.3 (exception references to Clauses 4 and 7) + Clauses 4 and 7
constraints.reasoning: Clause 2.3 carves out Clause 4/7 disclosures as permitted; thus those categories imply the disclosure is not 'without permission'.

constraints.translation: Undertaking to keep Confidential Information confidential implies undertaking not to disclose it except as permitted.
constraints.reasoning: Common-sense semantic entailment: confidentiality obligations typically include non-disclosure duties, consistent with the structure of Clause 2.
